title: THREAT Matrix Framework Schema
description: JSON Schema (3.0.0) for THREAT Matrix framework.json: an open behavioral vocabulary and evidence index for threat assessment. The document carries tactics, indicators, countermeasures, response protocols, actor profiles, and a bibliography. It carries no scores: the experimental, non-normative scoring overlay is a separate document with its own schema (scoring-overlay.schema.json). Field values describe a property of the indicator or tactic type, never of a specific case or assessment. See CONTRIBUTING.md "Schema design principles". Every object is closed. Patterns are plain anchored ECMA-262 expressions with no lookaround and no backreferences, so any regex engine can compile them. Under ECMA-262 the closing $ rejects a trailing newline; Python's re module is lenient there, so scripts/lint/validate.py re-checks every identifier and key with an exact full match.

version.description: Semantic version of the framework content release (SemVer 2.0.0, pattern-enforced).

schema_version.description: Semantic version of the schema this document targets. The pattern pins MAJOR 3, so a document declaring any other schema major is rejected while 3.x MINOR and PATCH values remain valid; scripts/lint/validate.py pins the exact value it was written for.

matrices.description: Four target matrices: person, facility, organization, infrastructure. Each matrix contains tactics and a scope sentence describing the primary threat actor objective that places a tactic in that matrix. The matrices container also carries a boundary_rule describing the framework-vs-operational partition principle. Each matrix is validated by its own per-matrix subschema: a matrix's tactics must carry that matrix's id prefix (TM/TF/TO/TI) AND a matrix field const-equal to the containing key, so a person tactic given a TF id or a matrix:'facility' field is rejected by schema alone.

boundary_rule.description: Framework-vs-operational boundary principle governing matrix placement. Authoring-time: one matrix per tactic, set by the threat actor's primary objective. Operational-time: real incidents may invoke tactics from multiple matrices via Detection Mesh cross-references (correlates_with at the indicator level). Type-level statement of the framework's organizing principle.

ai_architecture.description: AI capability vectors and amplification risk metadata.

bibliography.description: Central citation library. Each key is a unique reference ID; each value is a bibliographic entry. Keys follow the docs/IDENTIFIERS.md convention: uppercase letters and digits in hyphen-separated segments, starting with a letter, at least two segments, and never the shape of an indicator, countermeasure, or response-protocol ID (pattern-enforced). scripts/lint/validate.py additionally requires every entry to be cited by at least one source_refs.

phase_mappings.description: Cross-walk from THREAT Matrix phases to NTAC, Calhoun-Weston, CERT, Cyber Kill Chain, MITRE ATT&CK, and MITRE ATLAS stages. Enables AI/RAG cross-framework interoperability across physical, cyber, and AI-systems threat actor models.

detection_mesh.description: Architectural prose object describing the cross-cutting Detection Mesh property along five axes. The axes array carries each of the five named axes exactly once.

prose.description: A non-empty text value with no leading or trailing whitespace. Interior whitespace, including line breaks, is allowed.

semver.description: A SemVer 2.0.0 version string (the grammar published at semver.org, ASCII digits only).

tactic_id.description: Tactic ID: T, a matrix letter (M person, F facility, O organization, I infrastructure), a two-digit phase (01 to 04), and a two-digit sequence starting at 01.

indicator_id.description: Indicator ID: IND, an optional matrix letter (none for person), the parent tactic's four digits, and a two-digit sequence starting at 01.

countermeasure_id.description: Countermeasure ID, same grammar as an indicator ID with the CM prefix.

response_protocol_id.description: Response-protocol ID, same grammar as an indicator ID with the RP prefix.

actor_profile_id.description: Actor profile ID: AP and a three-digit sequence starting at 001.

bibliography_key.description: Bibliography key: uppercase letters and digits in hyphen-separated segments, starting with a letter, at least two segments. A string in the shape of an indicator, countermeasure, or response-protocol ID is not a legal key, so the namespaces cannot collide.

http_url.description: An http or https URL with no whitespace.

matrix_maturity.description: Maturity of a matrix. core: the matrix is part of the reviewed vocabulary. draft: the matrix is published for comment and may change without a deprecation cycle.

lifecycle_rules.description: The lifecycle contract shared by tactics, indicators, countermeasures, response protocols, and actor profiles (docs/DEPRECATION.md). active (or absent): no lifecycle detail field. deprecated: deprecated_in and deprecation_reason, no superseded_by. superseded: deprecated_in, deprecation_reason, and superseded_by. reserved (actor profiles only): reserved_reason and no other lifecycle detail field. reserved_reason is legal only in the reserved state.

matrix_scope.description: Canonical scope sentence for a matrix, expressed in WHAT/WHY/WHERE terms. Defines the primary threat actor objective that places a tactic in this matrix at authoring time. Type-level field; not case-specific. See matrices.boundary_rule for the framework-vs-operational distinction.

lifecycle_state.description: Optional lifecycle state per docs/DEPRECATION.md. When absent the tactic is active. deprecated requires deprecated_in and deprecation_reason. superseded requires those plus superseded_by. An active tactic carries none of the lifecycle detail fields. reserved is not a legal state here: in schema 3.0.0 only actor profiles may be reserved, and reserved identifiers of this namespace are recorded in the ID manifest's reserved list.

deprecated_in.description: Framework content version (SemVer) in which this tactic entered deprecated or superseded state. Required in those states, forbidden otherwise. scripts/lint/validate.py also rejects a value later than the document version.

superseded_by.description: Required when lifecycle_state is superseded, forbidden otherwise. Same-namespace ID of the replacement tactic. scripts/lint/validate.py requires the target to exist, to be active, and not to be this tactic itself, so a supersession chain cannot loop.

deprecation_reason.description: Brief explanation of a deprecated or superseded state, suitable for a CHANGELOG entry (docs/DEPRECATION.md). Required in those states, forbidden otherwise.

phase_name.description: Human-readable phase name. Fully determined by phase: 1 Target Development, 2 Mobilization, 3 Execution, 4 Aftermath (enforced by the conditionals on this object). The third and fourth characters of the tactic id encode the same phase.

phase_4_track.description: Aftermath sub-track for phase-4 tactics: 'evasion' (Evade: withdrawal, evidence management, cover, counter-forensics, re-attack positioning) or 'attribution' (Claim: declaring, amplifying, messaging, coercive leverage). Framework-level structure carried by every matrix's phase-4 tactics; required on phase 4 and forbidden on phases 1 to 3 (enforced by the conditionals on this object).

notes.description: Formal taxonomic description of the tactic.

observed_contexts.description: Generic context archetypes. Pattern archetypes only; never case names.

evidence_basis.description: Declares how the tactic was authored. practice_led: tactic structure and indicators were authored from practitioner experience, with public sources cited that corroborate the pattern. practice_and_literature: authored from practice and published literature together. literature_led: derived mainly from published literature with practitioner review. literature_only: derived from published literature with no practitioner origin claimed. Whatever the value, every tactic, indicator, countermeasure, and response protocol cites public sources only.

related_tactics.description: Tactic IDs related to this tactic. Each entry must be a tactic ID (pattern-enforced). scripts/lint/validate.py requires each entry to resolve to an existing tactic other than this one.

actor_associations.description: Actor profiles associated with this tactic. scripts/lint/validate.py requires each actor_id to resolve to a non-reserved actor profile and allows one entry per actor_id and employment_status pair.

source_refs.description: Bibliography keys, at least one. Each entry must match the bibliography key convention (pattern-enforced); resolution against the bibliography is checked by scripts/lint/validate.py.

assessment_guidance.description: Optional structured per-tactic assessment guidance; when present all six parts are required. Type-level inherent property of the tactic class; consumers cite the criteria preambles, high/low signal anchors, false-positive contexts, and threshold guidance to inform their own assessments. The criteria field on each of credibility/capability/intent/opportunity articulates the underlying judgment rule (e.g., 'Credibility rises with X, Y, Z; falls with A, B, C'); the high_signal_anchors and low_signal_anchors arrays illustrate the criteria with specific patterns and are indicative rather than exhaustive. Not a score and not case-specific. See CONTRIBUTING.md "Schema design principles".

criteria.description: Type-level prose preamble articulating the underlying credibility-judgment rule. Carries the contract; anchors illustrate it.

capability.description: Per-tactic aid for reading a specific actor's capability from evidence. Distinct from informs_axes.actor_capability, which records what observing the indicator class reveals about capability. The per-case judgment belongs in a case record, never in this document.

criteria.description: Type-level prose preamble articulating the underlying capability-judgment rule. Carries the contract; anchors illustrate it.
Type-level prose preamble articulating the underlying intent-judgment rule. Carries the contract; anchors illustrate it.
Type-level prose preamble articulating the underlying opportunity-judgment rule. Carries the contract; anchors illustrate it.

false_positive_context.description: Patterns where surface behavior matches the tactic's indicators but the underlying activity is legitimate. Criteria + contexts shape mirrors the credibility/capability/intent/opportunity sub-fields.

criteria.description: Type-level prose articulating what distinguishes a false-positive from a real concern. Carries the contract; contexts illustrate it.

threshold_guidance.description: Prose describing when the tactic's indicators warrant escalation to a threat assessment team.

target_identity_scope.description: Optional. Type-level declaration of which target_identity sub-classes this tactic's prose covers. Primarily meaningful for People matrix tactics. Authored per tactic based on actual prose coverage; tactics whose operational logic generalizes carry multiple values, tactics intrinsically narrow declare a single value. See target_identity on indicator for the per-indicator sub-dimension.

tactic_person.description: A tactic in the person matrix: the base tactic plus a matrix-specific id prefix and matrix const. Rejects a tactic placed under the wrong matrix key in schema alone.

tactic_facility.description: A tactic in the facility matrix: base tactic plus TF id prefix and matrix const 'facility'.

tactic_organization.description: A tactic in the organization matrix: base tactic plus TO id prefix and matrix const 'organization'.

tactic_infrastructure.description: A tactic in the infrastructure matrix: base tactic plus TI id prefix and matrix const 'infrastructure'.

lifecycle_state.description: Optional lifecycle state per docs/DEPRECATION.md. When absent the indicator is active. deprecated requires deprecated_in and deprecation_reason. superseded requires those plus superseded_by. An active indicator carries none of the lifecycle detail fields. reserved is not a legal state here: in schema 3.0.0 only actor profiles may be reserved, and reserved identifiers of this namespace are recorded in the ID manifest's reserved list.

deprecated_in.description: Framework content version (SemVer) in which this indicator entered deprecated or superseded state. Required in those states, forbidden otherwise. scripts/lint/validate.py also rejects a value later than the document version.

superseded_by.description: Required when lifecycle_state is superseded, forbidden otherwise. Same-namespace ID of the replacement indicator. scripts/lint/validate.py requires the target to exist, to be active, and not to be this indicator itself, so a supersession chain cannot loop.

deprecation_reason.description: Brief explanation of a deprecated or superseded state, suitable for a CHANGELOG entry (docs/DEPRECATION.md). Required in those states, forbidden otherwise.

correlates_with.description: Indicator IDs this behavior co-occurs with (Detection Mesh cross-correlation). Referents are indicator IDs only, within or across matrices; cross-matrix links are reviewed against the mesh link rule (docs/METHODOLOGY.md) before authoring. scripts/lint/validate.py requires each entry to resolve to an existing indicator other than this one.

modality.description: Intrinsic modality of the behavior, decided by the behavior's own mechanism, its INSTRUMENT, and the zone its access reaches; never its effect, target importance, or the venue it travels through. physical = matter, force, or presence is the instrument (kinetic/on-site/hand act); cyber = the instrument operates on a computing system's access, code, data, or machinery (a platform used merely as a communication channel does NOT qualify); cyber_physical = the behavior itself crosses the seam (a cyber action reaching/reading/writing the OT control plane, a physical implant gaining cyber reach, or a technical digital-or-electromagnetic means producing a physical-infrastructure effect); human_social = the instrument operates on people or institutions (persuasion, coercion, recruitment, legal or financial process) with no technical instrument, in which case the human_social boolean facet is necessarily true. CPN is NOT stored; it is computed over the Detection Mesh from crossings plus same-operation kill-chain membership.

crossing_mechanism.description: For modality=cyber_physical only: how the seam is crossed. digital = IT/network/software action reaches the OT control plane; electromagnetic = RF/GNSS/EW (jamming or spoofing of a signal a physical system depends on); physical_implant = a physical device placed to gain cyber reach.

human_social.description: Independent facet: true when the behavior's essence is influencing, recruiting, cultivating, coercing, deceiving, or negotiating with people, or is human warning-behavior leakage (grievance escalation, statements of intent, behavioral withdrawal), regardless of medium. Orthogonal to modality: a behavior may be human_social AND carry any modality value; a behavior whose modality IS human_social must carry human_social=true (schema-enforced).

temporal_signature.description: Type-level property of the indicator class describing how close to action it typically appears. Distinct from phase_relevance, which describes which lifecycle phase the indicator belongs to. Base values (horizon, advancing, imminent, staging, in_progress, aftermath) define primary pathway positions; optional _early / _late refinements are available for horizon, advancing, imminent, and aftermath where within-band variation carries meaningful operational signal. Staging and in_progress are not split (staging is already a tight terminal-prep window; in_progress is binary). Authors should use the base value when within-band position is ambiguous; use a granular variant only when the indicator class clearly clusters at the early or late edge of its band. Type-level inherent property; not case-specific. See CONTRIBUTING.md "Schema design principles".

informs_axes.description: Type-level metadata describing which axes of the larger threat picture this indicator class typically informs, and how finely. Optional; when present all six axes are required. Universal resolution scale (resolution, not severity): none = no signal on the axis; weak = resolves only the axis's coarsest grain (the axis-relevant fact exists); moderate = one grain finer (the coarse fact plus one narrowing); strong = resolves to a specific value. Rate the indicator class as written, type-level; never a vivid case instance. Six axes covering actor (capability / intent / opportunity) and the postulated event (timing / target / method). Categorical scale {strong, moderate, weak, none}; not numeric. The framework's collective judgment about how strongly an indicator class informs an axis is itself categorical at root; numeric values would be false precision. For AI/ML consumers needing continuous features, the documented mapping is strong=0.9, moderate=0.6, weak=0.3, none=0.0; this mapping is a downstream-consumer convention only and is not part of the vocabulary. See CONTRIBUTING.md "Schema design principles".

actor_capability.description: What observing the class REVEALS about the actor's skill, tradecraft, and operational sophistication; distinct from assessment_guidance.capability (a per-tactic aid for reading a specific actor's capability from evidence). Grains: none = purely passive/ambient behavior achievable with zero skill and zero deliberate effort (rare); weak = a deliberate action with no tradecraft visible; moderate = a real competence demonstrated (pretext durability, multi-modal coordination, concealed-imaging tradecraft, counter-surveillance); strong = advanced or specialized tradecraft (productive analysis of restricted artifacts, credential fabrication, manufacturing, regulatory-control defeat).

actor_intent.description: The actor's GENERAL intent-to-act, read at type level only: specific motive class is case-level and excluded. Grains: weak = diffuse or ambient adverse interest, not yet directed; moderate = purposive, directed attention toward the subject without clear commitment; strong = clear general intent-to-act (broad-to-narrow behavioral progression, operational specificity, retention of acquired materials, grievance paired with reconnaissance). Never raise to strong because a specific motive can be imagined.

actor_opportunity.description: The actor's opportunity, tiered rather than averaged across its two sub-meanings: weak = generic or ambient reach only; moderate = a resolved exploitable condition at the INFORMATIONAL tier (pattern-of-life knowledge, security-gap awareness); strong = REALIZED action-opportunity (an exploited insider relationship, direct unsupervised access, demonstrated reach within an exploitable window). During-execution support behaviors inherit the operation's realized opportunity (strong).

threat_timing.description: Proximity-to-action. Locked boundary: weak = phase-only (places the threat in a pathway phase with no finer resolution); moderate = phase plus something narrower (schedule-aligned behavior, operational-tempo cues); strong = pins a specific action window (imminent, dated, or event-aligned). Mobilization-phase rehearsal, probing, and attempted or actual breach/penetration behaviors read strong; concealment and OPSEC behaviors are excepted (weak).

threat_target.description: Which specific target or asset is in view. Grains: weak = targeting at a target-class level only; moderate = narrowed to a candidate set or subject-associated locations; strong = the specific named subject or subject-specific assets, including behaviors tied to a specific target-associated environment.

threat_method.description: How the attack would be conducted: the ATTACK method only: access and approach tradecraft does not inform method (reads none or weak). All execution in framework scope is physical; never treat physical-vs-digital as a narrowing (digital reconnaissance still describes a physical attack downstream). Grains: none = method-agnostic, all physical methods remain in play; weak = barely narrows the physical-methods space; moderate = narrows to 2 to 3 candidate physical methods; strong = pins a specific physical method (e.g., VBIED, hostage scenario, targeted assassination).

target_identity.description: Optional multi-select sub-dimension within the People matrix: the victim identity-class(es) this indicator class REVEALS (revealed reading; tag only what the behavior actually indicates; empty/absent = reveals nothing about victim identity). named_individual = one OR MORE specific pre-identified persons are the object; surveillance/profiling/approach/force/seizure/captivity/leverage directed at the person(s), OR a specific target-associated site/environment/route coupled to them (a site reveals that specific known person(s), singular or plural, are the target). role_or_identity_category = selection is by role/what-they-are (a judge, cops by uniform, clinic staff, journalists). affinity_group = a cohesive group property selects the victims (demographic, religious, ethnic; e.g. worshippers, a gathering). indiscriminate = anyone / random crowd, no selection filter (mass-casualty by proximity/availability). Empty/absent = the behavior class reveals nothing about victim identity (capability acquisition, breach/access mechanics, OPSEC/tradecraft, logistics, financing, evidence management, most aftermath evasion). Coupling rule: tag only when observing the class resolves WHO the victim is; the person(s) or their coupled site/environment; behaviors that merely presuppose a victim without revealing the class stay empty.

facility_target_scope.description: Optional Facility-matrix sub-dimension: the breadth of site selection this indicator class REVEALS about the actor (revealed reading: tag only what the behavior actually indicates, not what it could apply to; empty/absent = reveals nothing about breadth). specific_site = one identified building (grievance tied to a named facility, surveillance of a specific building, as-built drawings of this site). site_class = any facility of a FUNCTIONAL/OPERATIONAL type: grouped by what the site does (any branch of an org, any hospital, any transit hub, clinics/schools of a type). symbolic_category = any site of an IDEOLOGICALLY/SYMBOLICALLY-defined category: grouped by what the site represents (any government building, any place of worship of a faith, landmarks). The discriminator between site_class and symbolic_category is the BASIS OF GROUPING (function vs meaning), not specificity; both are breadth values (any member of the group). A single named site chosen for symbolic motive is specific_site, not symbolic_category. indiscriminate = any accessible site, opportunistic with no site preference. The Facility parallel to the People matrix `target_identity`; captures breadth (which/how many sites) distinct from victim count and from informs_axes.threat_target (how well the indicator resolves the target). TARGET-COUPLING RULE: populate only when the behavior reveals the breadth of an ACTUAL target selection; general knowledge, capability, or method acquisition not coupled to a target or target-class carries no scope (empty). SYMBOLIC RULE: symbolic_category applies only when symbolism defines the target BREADTH (a category chosen for its meaning); symbolic MOTIVE for a named or class target does not make it symbolic_category: a specific building chosen for what it represents is specific_site. MULTI-TAG RULE: assign multiple values only when the behavior text explicitly spans breadths, or the observable behavior independently supports each: never because several possibilities can be inferred.

within_site_focus.description: Optional Facility-matrix sub-dimension: what inside the facility the indicator class REVEALS as the harm focus (revealed reading; empty/absent = unresolved). structure = the building/physical asset (arson, structural sabotage, defacement, demolition). occupants = the people inside (mass-casualty intent, hostage-taking, active-shooter positioning). systems = utilities/controls/functional systems whose defeat or contamination is the aim (power, water, HVAC/contamination, fire/security-system defeat that is the attack itself: NOT security-system defeat merely to gain access). whole_site = the site as an undifferentiated unit (seizure/occupation, generic threat against the facility). Decision rule for occupied-structure attacks: `occupants` when casualty intent is shown, `structure` when the aim is property/denial with incidental casualties, both only when the behavior genuinely reveals both aims. Facility-native (no People analog); load-bearing for triage. AIM-COUPLING RULE: populate only when the behavior reveals the within-site OBJECT OF HARM. Recon of site dimensions (floor plans, layout, security posture), method/capability acquisition (breaching tools, accelerants, ramming vehicles), and general technical literacy carry no focus (empty) unless explicitly coupled to a within-site aim. Floor-plan/layout study is recon, NOT a structure focus: reserve `structure` for load-bearing/collapse/destruction aims; reserve `systems` for utility/HVAC/fire-system defeat that is the attack itself.

conditioning_guidance.description: Framework-provided default investigative-tasking guidance for conditioning this indicator at instance time: which instance factors to probe (probe_factors, machine-filterable) and a natural-language directive (guidance). Assessment-scoped only: immediate response actions (alerting, notification, mitigation) are carried by the tactic's response_protocols, never by this field. A starting point, NOT a complete or prescriptive instruction: consumers may follow, extend, or override it with their own playbooks. Intended for composition across combinations of observed indicators (see detection_mesh / correlates_with), not single-indicator reading. Type-level.

probe_factors.description: Machine-readable index of the instance factors this indicator's guidance points at. Enum names are the six instance factors of the case record (docs/data/case-record.schema.json, instance_factors).

guidance.description: Natural-language practitioner directive: what to go collect and why it decides how dangerous the case is. No dash-like punctuation: figure dash, en dash, em dash, horizontal bar, and minus sign (U+2012 to U+2015, U+2212) are rejected by pattern.

lifecycle_state.description: Optional lifecycle state per docs/DEPRECATION.md. When absent the countermeasure is active. deprecated requires deprecated_in and deprecation_reason. superseded requires those plus superseded_by. An active countermeasure carries none of the lifecycle detail fields. reserved is not a legal state here: in schema 3.0.0 only actor profiles may be reserved, and reserved identifiers of this namespace are recorded in the ID manifest's reserved list.

deprecated_in.description: Framework content version (SemVer) in which this countermeasure entered deprecated or superseded state. Required in those states, forbidden otherwise. scripts/lint/validate.py also rejects a value later than the document version.

superseded_by.description: Required when lifecycle_state is superseded, forbidden otherwise. Same-namespace ID of the replacement countermeasure. scripts/lint/validate.py requires the target to exist, to be active, and not to be this countermeasure itself, so a supersession chain cannot loop.

deprecation_reason.description: Brief explanation of a deprecated or superseded state, suitable for a CHANGELOG entry (docs/DEPRECATION.md). Required in those states, forbidden otherwise.

compensates_for.description: Countermeasure-to-countermeasure compensation: this countermeasure compensates for the ABSENCE or failure of the referenced countermeasure (redundancy relation). Indicator coverage does NOT live here; it lives in mitigates. An IND- referent in this field is a type error.

function.description: How this countermeasure acts on the behavior's pathway: prevent (stops the act), detect (surfaces the act), deny (removes the act's value). Authored per edge, never inherited from the countermeasure. 'unreviewed' is a provisional value for edges whose function has not yet been reviewed; under the coverage contract (coverage.schema.json) an unreviewed or detect-only edge caps coverage at partial.

mitigates.description: The countermeasure-to-indicator mitigation relation: this countermeasure prevents, detects, or denies the referenced behavior, per the linking criterion (acts on the behavior's pathway; same-tactic membership is not sufficient; cross-tactic edges are expected where a countermeasure genuinely reaches). This relation is the input to coverage derivation (coverage.schema.json). scripts/lint/validate.py requires each edge to resolve to an existing indicator and allows one edge per indicator.

target_identity.description: Optional. Mirror of indicator target_identity for the small set of person-matrix countermeasures whose coverage is scoped by victim identity-class. Same enum and multi-select semantics as indicator.target_identity.

lifecycle_state.description: Optional lifecycle state per docs/DEPRECATION.md. When absent the response protocol is active. deprecated requires deprecated_in and deprecation_reason. superseded requires those plus superseded_by. An active response protocol carries none of the lifecycle detail fields. reserved is not a legal state here: in schema 3.0.0 only actor profiles may be reserved, and reserved identifiers of this namespace are recorded in the ID manifest's reserved list.

deprecated_in.description: Framework content version (SemVer) in which this response protocol entered deprecated or superseded state. Required in those states, forbidden otherwise. scripts/lint/validate.py also rejects a value later than the document version.

superseded_by.description: Required when lifecycle_state is superseded, forbidden otherwise. Same-namespace ID of the replacement response protocol. scripts/lint/validate.py requires the target to exist, to be active, and not to be this response protocol itself, so a supersession chain cannot loop.

deprecation_reason.description: Brief explanation of a deprecated or superseded state, suitable for a CHANGELOG entry (docs/DEPRECATION.md). Required in those states, forbidden otherwise.

coordinates_with.description: Response-protocol IDs that co-activate on overlapping indicator sets (Detection Mesh co-activation). A directed dependency layer (gates / precedes / deconflicts) is the committed evolution of this relation.

lifecycle_state.description: Optional lifecycle state per docs/DEPRECATION.md. When absent the actor profile is active. deprecated requires deprecated_in and deprecation_reason. superseded requires those plus superseded_by. An active actor profile carries none of the lifecycle detail fields. reserved is legal on actor profiles only: a reserved profile carries id, lifecycle_state, and reserved_reason and nothing else.

deprecated_in.description: Framework content version (SemVer) in which this actor profile entered deprecated or superseded state. Required in those states, forbidden otherwise. scripts/lint/validate.py also rejects a value later than the document version.

superseded_by.description: Required when lifecycle_state is superseded, forbidden otherwise. Same-namespace ID of the replacement actor profile. scripts/lint/validate.py requires the target to exist, to be active, and not to be this actor profile itself, so a supersession chain cannot loop.

deprecation_reason.description: Brief explanation of a deprecated or superseded state, suitable for a CHANGELOG entry (docs/DEPRECATION.md). Required in those states, forbidden otherwise.

reserved_reason.description: Required when lifecycle_state is reserved, forbidden otherwise. Brief explanation of why the identifier slot is held.

category_label.description: Human-readable label for the actor category. Fixed by category (enforced by the conditionals on this object).

awareness.description: Whether the actor is aware of / intends the threat activity (e.g. witting vs unwitting).

direction.description: Directionality of the actor relative to the protected entity (e.g. internal vs external).

access_relationship.description: The actor's access relationship to the target (insider access, trusted third party, outsider, etc.).

phase_compression_risk.description: Type-level note on this actor class's tendency to compress the attack lifecycle phases.

actor_level.description: Sophistication / resourcing tier of the actor class.

attack_vectors.description: Attack vectors typically available to this actor class.

primary_matrices.description: Target matrices this actor class primarily operates against.

behavioral_markers.description: Observable behavioral markers characteristic of this actor class.

ai_enabled_risks.description: AI-specific risk amplifiers applicable to this actor class (may be empty). See ai_architecture.vectors.ai_enabled_risks.

v2_tactic_associations.description: Optional. Held for profile-to-tactic associations. When populated, each entry names a tactic ID and a relevance, mirroring actor_association in the opposite direction; scripts/lint/validate.py requires each tactic_id to resolve.

insider_type.description: Optional. Present on insider actor classes (e.g. malicious / negligent / compromised).

insider_subtype.description: Optional. Finer insider classification (e.g. recruited / coerced / unwitting).

employment_status.description: Optional. Employment status of the insider actor class (e.g. current).

state_actor_type.description: Optional. Present on state-actor classes (e.g. direct / proxy / front / sponsored).

date.description: Publication date: YYYY, YYYY-MM, YYYY-MM-DD, a year range YYYY-YYYY, or n.d. (optionally followed by an access date in the form n.d. (accessed YYYY-MM-DD)).

url.description: Public location of the source, or null when none exists. http and https only; every other scheme is rejected.

doi.description: Bare DOI (10.NNNN/suffix, no resolver prefix), or null.

matrices.description: Optional. Which target matrices this source supports/informs. Enables consumers to pull sourcing by matrix and the UI to group the bibliography by matrix. A source may support multiple matrices; tagging (not partitioning) keeps flat key-based citation intact.

topics.description: Optional. Attack-method / subject tags for filtering sources by need (e.g., bombing, arson, structural_sabotage, forced_entry, vehicle_ramming, soft_targets, target_selection, cbrn_contamination, cyber_physical, building_systems_sabotage, occupation_siege, symbolic_ideological, active_shooter, insider_threat, mass_attack, threat_assessment, protective_intelligence, risk_methodology, physical_protection_systems, incident_data, financial_crime). Free-string to allow extension; the listed vocabulary is the recommended starter set.
